list: Audio tour system with eye tracking feature, which offers commentary based on where the visitor is looking. No commentary file has been installed, though, so all it plays is the test music track.

Filled with advertising brochures and guide booklets, dated to the museum's opening day. The date matters little. The exhibits are so brilliant that visitors' eyes barely have time to linger upon the brochures.
The fence seems to block the path, but there is plenty of space to go around. The concept is simple: Reynell believes that anyone who gets turned away by this does not deserve to enter.
Panoramic display that shows the exterior of the Galería Krysztauowa, even simulating the water stains and dust on the glass wall. It does not show the pool full of golf balls, however.
Flooring used in the Galería Krysztauowa, somewhat modest compared to the rest of the furnishing. The light-colored marble does not help one relax, but instead makes things seem more distant.

Part of the Galería Krysztauowa collection, created by an Ægir who lived in Iberia. At first, it was seen as embodying the determination of humanity to conquer the oceans; later, it was seen as premonition of the disaster.
theme: Concept room that recreates a private gallery in the Galería Krysztauowa, displaying replicas of the artwork there.
